 Kirti Singh. J.(Oral)

This is the second petition filed under Section 483 BNSS Act for grant of regular bail to the petitioner in case FIR No.496 dated 21.08.2023, under Sections 363, 366A, 376(2)(n), 420, 506 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act, registered at Police Station Adampur, District Hisar.

The first bail petition was dismissed as withdrawn on 09.09.2024.
2.

The contents of the aforesaid FIR are reproduced herein below:-
"

Statement of xxx daughter of Ramesh Kumar, Caste SC (Dhanak), Resident of Village Adampur, District Hisar, Age 16 years, Education 12th, Mobile Number xxx stated that I am a resident of the aforementioned address.
We are two sisters, my elder sister is xxx, and I am younger than her.
I study in the 12th class at Government Girls Senior Secondary School, Village Adampur.

sentences.text: I know Kuldeep son of Mahender resident of Village Adampur for about three years, and he lives a short distance from my house.

for about two years, we did not have any contact.

Then, about six months ago,
Kuldeep sent me a message on Instagram.
I did not respond to his messages, but he kept messaging me repeatedly.
Fed up, I started talking to him, and we became friends.
Kuldeep took advantage of our friendship and, for about a month, kept pressuring me to meet him and repeatedly asked me to meet, but I kept refusing.
On 23/07/23, Kuldeep lured me, took me on his motorcycle, and around 2:40 PM, took me to Swagat Bar and Restaurant Hotel in Adampur.
There, he repeatedly pressured me to engage in wrong acts, but I refused.
Then Kuldeep threatened me, saying that if I told anyone about this, he would kill me, and then he dropped me near my house.
He also said that if I didn't comply with him, he would defame me.

Due to his threats,
on 06/08/23, around 12:30 PM, out of fear, I went with Kuldeep on his motorcycle HR20AP-3600, Hero Honda, black in color to Swagat Bar and Restaurant Hotel in Mandi Adampur.
There, in the hotel room, Kuldeep forcibly committed rape on me multiple times against my will.
When I started crying, he threatened me, saying that if I told my family about this, he would kill my family.
He then dropped me near my house around 5:00 PM and fled.
Kuldeep recorded a video of us kissing in the hotel that day and also took photos, and I am afraid that he might make the video and photos viral.
Strict action should be taken against Kuldeep.
I have given my statement without any pressure in the presence of my mother, xxx, and female advocate xxx.
I have read and heard my statement, and it is correct."

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present FIR, which was registered after a considerable delay of 15 days on the statement of the prosecutrix made under pressure, wherein she levelled baseless allegations against him.

It is further submitted that the petitioner and the prosecutrix were well known to each other being neighbours,
and had been in contact through Instagram for over 06 months prior to the alleged incident.
Further, there is no medical evidence on record that indicates towards the complicity of the petitioner.

In fact, credibility and reliability of the forensic KAVITA NAIN 2025.11.04 14:04 I agree to specified portions of this document CRM-M-60080-2025(O&M)
- 3- evidence is also questionable, particularly in the absence of any DNA report, given the considerable delay in the collection of samples since date of alleged incident i.e. 06.08.2023, while the registration of the FIR and the subsequent medical of prosecutrix was done on 21/22.08.2023.
The petitioner, aged 22 years has undergone an actual custody of 02 years and 02 months.
He has clean antecedents and there is no other case registered against him.
4. Per contra, learned State counsel has vehemently opposed the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
He has filed custody certificate in Court today and the same is taken on record.
As per custody certificate, the petitioner has undergone an actual custody of 02 years and 02 months and there is no other case registered against the present petitioner.
He on instructions from SI Sheesh Pal, submits that the charges were framed on 27.03.2024 and out of a total of 21 prosecution witnesses, only four have been examined till date.
He, however, submits that in view of the serious allegations against the petitioner, petitioner is not entitled to the concession of regular bail.

sentences.text: 5. Heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties.
6. From a perusal of the case in hand, it transpires that the petitioner is behind the bars since 03.09.2023.
Investigation is complete.

The final report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. was presented before the concerned Court and trial of the case has not made much progress, as charges were framed on 27.03.2024 and out of a total of 21 prosecution witnesses, only four have been examined till date.
However, the material witnesses stand examined.
The culpability, if any, would be determined at the time of trial.
No useful purpose shall be served by further detention of the accused/petitioner.

Keeping the petitioner in further detention KAVITA NAIN 2025.11.04 14:04 I agree to specified portions of this document CRM-M-60080-2025(O&M)
- 4- without the prospect of the trial being concluded in the near future, would be violative of his rights under Article 21 of the Constitution of India including the right to speedy trial, and is against the principle "Bail is a rule, jail is an exception" as elucidated in the judgment of Apex Court in "Dataram Singh vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another", (2018) 3 SCC 22.
7.

sentences.text: Without commenting anything on the merits of the case, lest it may prejudice the trial, the present petition is allowed and the petitioner is ordered to be released on regular bail on his furnishing adequate bail/surety bonds to the satisfaction of the concerned learned trial Court/Duty Magistrate.

The petitioner shall also abide by the following conditions:-
(I) The petitioner will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(II) The petitioner will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witness(s).
(III) The petitioner will appear before the trial Court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
(IV) The petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused of, or for commission of which he is suspected.

(V) The petitioner shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
8.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move an application for cancellation of bail before this Court.
9. However, nothing stated above shall be construed as a final expression of opinion on the merits of the case and the trial Court would proceed
